chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That he disliked for the man that he eats with his left hand, or drinks with it, or takes (something) with it.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating and drinking with the left hand?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the dislike (karahah) of using the left hand for eating, drinking, and handling items, reinforcing the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often understood as recommended etiquette (adab) rather than strict prohibition, emphasizing physical cleanliness and spiritual mindfulness in daily acts of worship. The chain of transmission highlights the continuity of this practice through the Ahl al-Bayt, linking personal hygiene to broader theological concepts of purity (taharah).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman from Jarrah Al Madainy,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having disliked for the man that he eats by his left hand, or drinks by it, or takes (something) by it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mada’iniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
he dislikes for a man to eat with his left hand or drink with it and take something with it.”’
